info.name: F&B HQ API
info.description: Health, outlets, master menu, assignments, inventory, outlet menu, sales. Run top to bottom (Collection Runner) — later requests use ids saved by earlier ones. Each run creates new test rows (no DELETE API by design). Needs the seed (npm run db:seed) for DHA/GUL/UTT checks.

request.description: 200 with db up. Stop Postgres (5433) and re-send → 503 DB_UNAVAILABLE.

item.name: 1. Outlets
item.description: Rules 1–2: unique name/code, code format, counter created with the outlet, code immutable.

request.description: Rule 1–2. Pre-request generates a unique name and a random lowercase code for this run.

exec: let c = ""; for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) c += "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"[Math.floor(Math.random() * 26)];
pm.test("contains the new outlet", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.some(o => o.id === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("outletId")))).to.be.true; });
pm.test("sorted by id", () => { const ids = pm.response.json().data.map(o => o.id); pm.expect(ids).to.eql([...ids].sort((a, b) => a - b)); });

request.description: Code is printed on existing receipts, so it can't change.

item.name: 2. Menu items
item.description: Rule 3: unique sku, basePrice ≥ 0 with max 2 decimals. Money returned as string. No delete (rule 10).

exec: pm.test("contains the new item", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.some(i => i.id === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("menuItemId")))).to.be.true; });
pm.test("money is a string", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.every(i => typeof i.basePrice === "string")).to.be.true; });
pm.test("includes the inactive test item", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.some(i => i.id === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("inactiveItemId")))).to.be.true; });

item.name: 3. Assignments
item.description: Rules 4–10: assign + inventory row (qty 0), override, effective price, unassign via isAvailable. No DELETE.

request.description: Rules 4–5: creates the assignment AND its inventory row (stock 0) in one transaction.
Rules 6–7: effectivePrice = priceOverride ?? basePrice.
Rule 10: unassign = isAvailable false. No DELETE.

item.name: List still shows the unavailable item

exec: pm.test("item listed with isAvailable false", () => { const a = pm.response.json().data.find(x => x.menuItemId === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("menuItemId"))); pm.expect(a.isAvailable).to.be.false; });

request.description: Re-assigning is a PATCH isAvailable=true, POST stays 409.
Looks up GUL's id so the next request works on any machine.

exec: pm.test("GUL exists (run npm run db:seed)", () => { pm.expect(Boolean(gul)).to.be.true; });

request.description: Seeded Masala Chai at GUL: basePrice 60, override 80 → effective 80. Chicken Puri is unassigned but still listed for HQ.

exec: pm.test("Chicken Puri listed as unavailable", () => { pm.expect(rows.find(r => r.sku === "CPURI-01").isAvailable).to.be.false; });

item.name: 5. Inventory
item.description: Rules 11–16: stock per item, restock (+q), adjust (absolute, delta logged), logs newest first. Uses the item assigned in folder 3 (starts at stock 0).

exec: pm.test("assigned item listed with quantity 0", () => { const r = pm.response.json().data.find(x => x.menuItemId === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("menuItemId"))); pm.expect(r.quantity).to.eql(0); });

request.description: Rule 14: atomic increment + RESTOCK log; balanceAfter comes from the DB.

exec: pm.test("RESTOCK log +10 / 10", () => { const l = pm.response.json().data.log; pm.expect([l.changeType, l.quantityChange, l.balanceAfter, l.note]).to.eql(["RESTOCK", 10, 10, "Morning delivery"]); });

request.description: Rule 15: absolute value; logged delta = new − old = −6.

exec: pm.test("ADJUSTMENT log −6 / 4", () => { const l = pm.response.json().data.log; pm.expect([l.changeType, l.quantityChange, l.balanceAfter]).to.eql(["ADJUSTMENT", -6, 4]); });

item.name: Adjust to same value → no log

request.description: Invariant: sum of quantityChange = current quantity (4).

exec: pm.test("2 logs, newest first", () => { pm.expect(logs.map(l => l.changeType)).to.eql(["ADJUSTMENT", "RESTOCK"]); });
pm.test("Σ quantityChange = 4", () => { pm.expect(logs.reduce((s, l) => s + l.quantityChange, 0)).to.eql(4); });

item.name: 6. Outlet menu
item.description: Rules 7–9: only assigned + available + active items, effective price, sorted by name. Outlet-facing (POS).

exec: for (const c of ["DHA", "GUL", "UTT"]) { const o = all.find(x => x.code === c); if (o) pm.collectionVariables.set(c.toLowerCase() + "OutletId", o.id); }
pm.test("all 3 seeded outlets exist (run npm run db:seed)", () => { ["DHA", "GUL", "UTT"].forEach(c => pm.expect(Boolean(all.find(x => x.code === c))).to.be.true); });

pm.test("items + prices (sorted by name)", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.map(i => [i.name, i.price])).to.eql([["Dudh Cha","40.00"],["Lemon Tea","50.00"],["Malai Chai","90.00"],["Masala Chai","60.00"],["Singara","20.00"]]); });
pm.test("Malai Chai out of stock (inStock false)", () => { const m = pm.response.json().data.find(i => i.sku === "MALAI-01"); pm.expect([m.stock, m.inStock]).to.eql([0, false]); });

pm.test("items + prices (sorted by name)", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.map(i => [i.name, i.price])).to.eql([["Cold Coffee","150.00"],["Malai Chai","90.00"],["Masala Chai","80.00"],["Samosa","25.00"]]); });

pm.test("items + prices (sorted by name)", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.map(i => [i.name, i.price])).to.eql([["Dudh Cha","35.00"],["Lemon Tea","50.00"],["Samosa","25.00"],["Singara","20.00"]]); });

item.name: Test outlet menu shows the test item

request.description: Item from folder 3 (basePrice 19.99, stock 4 after folder 5).

exec: pm.test("price 19.99, stock 4, inStock", () => { const r = pm.response.json().data.find(i => i.menuItemId === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("menuItemId"))); pm.expect([r.price, r.stock, r.inStock]).to.eql(["19.99", 4, true]); });
let c = ""; for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) c += "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"[Math.floor(Math.random() * 26)];

request.description: Outlet exists but sells nothing yet: 200 with an empty list, not 404.

item.name: 7. Sales
item.description: Rules 17–28: one transaction, server prices, atomic stock, gapless receipts per outlet, clientId idempotency. Uses the test outlet/item (19.99, stock 4).

request.description: Price comes from the server (19.99), total = 2 × 19.99. First sale of a new outlet → CODE-000001.

exec: pm.test("line: qty 2 × 19.99 = 39.98", () => { const l = pm.response.json().data.items[0]; pm.expect([l.quantity, l.unitPrice, l.lineTotal]).to.eql([2, "19.99", "39.98"]); });

request.description: Rule 18: two lines of the same item become one line.

exec: pm.test("one merged line qty 2", () => { const items = pm.response.json().data.items; pm.expect([items.length, items[0].quantity]).to.eql([1, 2]); });

request.description: Rule 20: stock is now 0; whole sale fails, nothing changes, no receipt number used.

exec: pm.test("details: requested 1, available 0", () => { const d = pm.response.json().error.details; pm.expect([d.requested, d.available]).to.eql([1, 0]); });

item.name: Next sale → 000003 (failed sale used no number)

request.description: Rule 28: the 409 above rolled back, so numbering continues without a gap.
Rule 23: SALE log −1, balanceAfter 4.

exec: pm.test("newest log = SALE −1 / 4 with saleId", () => { const l = pm.response.json().data[0]; pm.expect([l.changeType, l.quantityChange, l.balanceAfter, typeof l.saleId]).to.eql(["SALE", -1, 4, "number"]); });

request.description: Rule 25: offline POS sends its own UUID as clientId.
Re-sent offline sale: returns the existing sale, no second sale, no extra stock deduction.
Rule 21: prices are never taken from the client.
